quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press down hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors for traffic before you stop. Be aware of other drivers. Release the accelerator and move your foot to the brake. Press the brake steadily for a smooth stop.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. Wait until they finish crossing before you go.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses before you go.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let any vehicle, bicycle rider, or pedestrian in the intersection go first. If a pedestrian is crossing, wait until they finish before you go.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped ahead with its red lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: Before driving after taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor if it affects your driving ability.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor if it affects your driving ability.
questions.explanation: Medicines can affect your driving. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving after taking any medicine. This is especially important for tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black words means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads where passing is not allowed.

questions.question: When should you let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave to you first.
Only if pedestrians are not using their phone.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to let any vehicle or pedestrian cross. Go only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags:

options.text: You should still wear seat belts.
You do not need to wear seat belts.
You should wear seat belts behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should still wear seat belts.
questions.explanation: Airbags are safety devices. For the best protection, wear your lap and shoulder belts along with airbags.

questions.question: This red and white sign means you should:

options.text: Stop and check both directions before going.
Let traffic on the road you are entering or crossing go first.
Keep the same speed and check all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you are entering or crossing go first.
questions.explanation: A three-sided yield sign means slow down and be ready to stop. Let any vehicle, bicycle rider, or pedestrian pass. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You should always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should let you go first.
You should never let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians cross first. Turn only when the intersection is clear and the signal allows.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to let the car slow down. Apply the brakes gently when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed a lot.

questions.question: This sign shows:

options.text: A right turn.
An intersection.
A lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and be ready to yield or stop before turning right or left.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: All drivers must respect other road users and follow the rules to stay safe and avoid crashes. When you see an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to get out of their way. Never try to compete with other drivers.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions coming up ahead. There may be a change in traffic direction, a steep downgrade, or another hazard that needs your attention.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let cross traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: When you see this sign, you must yield the right-of-way. Slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians cross in front of you before proceeding. Stop if needed.

questions.question: Your reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your eyesight and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distance, speed, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: To help others see you when it gets dark, you should use your:

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: As it gets dark, turn on your low beams so others can see you. Use your high beam headlights only when no other drivers are around.

questions.question: Delaware law does not say who has the right-of-way. Instead, it says:

options.text: Who must yield the right-of-way.
Nothing about the right-of-way.
Right-of-way does not exist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Delaware's motor vehicle laws do not give anyone the right-of-way. The law explains who must yield the right-of-way to others.

questions.question: You should not stop suddenly in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop and speed up than small vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time and could hit you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You are approaching the end of a divided highway.
You are approaching the start of a divided highway.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are approaching the start of a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting ahead. Stay to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Nothing else—like eating or drinking—can speed this up.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, even if there is no crosswalk.

questions.question: In a vehicle with airbags, where should children age 12 and under sit?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can be dangerous for children. Anyone age 12 or under should sit in the back seat.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signs. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to a winding road ahead. Slow down accordingly.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you:

options.text: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
Will always stop at the upcoming railroad crossing.
Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before crossing.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seatbelt, and secure items. Do not adjust mirrors while moving.

questions.question: An orange-colored sign like this means:

options.text: There is roadwork ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark construction areas. Drive carefully.

questions.question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads reduce tire grip. Slow down in these conditions.
